old: The elephant is of massive body, and he is under the goad's control: is the goad only the size of an elephant? When a lamp is lit, darkness vanishes: is darkness only the size of a lamp? Even struck by a thunderbolt, mountains fall: are the mountains only the size of a thunderbolt? He in whom brilliance shines is strong: what trust is there in the massive?
new: The elephant is of massive body, and he is under the goad's control: is the goad only the size of an elephant? When a lamp is lit, darkness vanishes: is darkness only the size of a lamp? Even struck by a thunderbolt, mountains fall: are the mountains only the size of a thunderbolt? He whose brilliance shines is strong: what trust is there in the massive?
why: reviewer (error): yasya tejaḥ virājate is genitive ('whose brilliance shines'); 'in whom' turns it into a locative and changes the case sense (Hindi जिसका is right).

old: With uncultivated fruits and roots, delighting always in living in the forest, he performs śrāddha day after day; that brahmin is called a sage.
new: Uncultivated fruits and roots, delighting always in living in the forest, he performs śrāddha day after day; that brahmin is called a sage.
why: reviewer (error): 'With' is added; the Sanskrit has a bare accusative plural. Even though disclosed in the notes, it is an added word that fixes the relation.

new: Translation of lines c and d is tentative: the syntax of asmākaṃ ... nāthaṃ cirāt saṃcitaṃ ... iti is unclear, the two flagged forms are doubtful, and nirvāṇāt 'from extinction' is kept literal. makṣikā can also mean flies. śrīkarṇasya may be a single name or Śrī (honorific) with Karṇa; vikramapateḥ is read as 'lord of valour' and could be a name or an epithet.
